_comment: Feather segmentation settings (src/feather_processing.py). A Celery task or sample run can override any key with options={'segmentation': {...}} without redeploying. sam3.imgsz needs a worker restart; everything else applies per task. feather_judge = the per-feather checks (score computed from them, see feather_judge.score); inventory = slide-level check for feathers the segmentation may have missed (review flags only, never a new letter or feather ID). The old slide_judge (metadata + a 1-10 overlay score) is retired: the label extractor owns Bird_ID/Date, and the inventory + per-feather checks cover what it asked. sam3.exemplar / sam3.refine: optional SAM 3 steps after the text prompt (src/sam3_extras.py, docs/sam3-segmentation-plan.md).

cleanup._comment: Glue and card removed from a mask before cropping (src/mask_cleanup.py): textureless patches touching the mask's edge (structure-tensor coherence below `coherence`) are cut off with everything below them when in the bottom `base_frac` of the feather, else removed; a narrow quill neck with a blob `neck_blob_ratio` times wider below it is cut at the neck. The crop's bottom is the higher of the cut and the trim line. The calamus (bare quill) is cut on every feather where the mask narrows to the quill's own width; the older vane_base cut (on the card, where the vane narrows below half its width) is off: it cut real vane (A1159 1998-im1266 C/D, A1383 2000-im1316 B).

feather_judge.prompt:
Reply with only the JSON object described at the end: no explanation, reasoning or text before or after it.

You are checking the segmentation of ONE feather on a scanned specimen slide. The image has two panels.
LEFT: the slide around this feather, with the segmentation outline drawn as a thin green line (green lines inside the feather mark holes in the segmentation). Other feathers and the slide background may also be visible.
RIGHT: exactly the pixels inside that outline, on black. Anything black in the RIGHT panel is NOT in the segmentation.

Compare the two panels and answer every check. Judge only what you can see; do not assume anything that is not visible.
When you are unsure about a check, give the answer that flags a problem ("cut", or true; for single_feather, false). A person looks at every flagged feather; a wrong pass is never looked at again.

The bottom of the feather may be cut off on purpose (the quill, glue and the thin lower vane on the card are removed): the bottom of the outline may then be a straight horizontal line across the feather or its quill. That straight cut is not a fault: answer "complete" for the bottom when the only cut there is that straight line, and do not count it as a fragment; ignore everything below it.

1. Outline, side by side: for each side of this feather as it appears in the image (left, right, top, bottom), answer "cut" if any visible part of THIS feather (vane, barbs, fringe, tip, shaft or base, including pale, white or translucent parts) extends beyond the green line on that side; otherwise answer "complete". A part hidden under something else on the slide (card, board, tape, another feather) does not count as cut.
2. Holes and gaps: answer true if any part of this feather inside its outline is missing from the RIGHT panel (a hole, gap, notch or band that is black on the RIGHT but feather on the LEFT), or if the segmentation is split into separate pieces. Natural separations between barbs that look the same on both panels are not holes.
3. One feather: single_feather is true only if the outline holds exactly one feather; fragment is true if it holds only a piece of a feather while the rest of that feather is visible outside it.
4. Nothing else: other_feather_inside is true if any part of a different feather is inside the outline, however small. other_material_inside is true if anything that is not feather (slide background, card, board, tape, label, glue, shadow) is inside the outline beyond a thin rim. A thin rim is a band of background that follows the outline and is only a few pixels wide (no wider than about twice the green line). A wider band, or a patch of background anywhere that does not follow the outline, counts as other material.

Answer with JSON only, no other text:
{"outline": {"left": "complete"|"cut", "right": "complete"|"cut", "top": "complete"|"cut", "bottom": "complete"|"cut"}, "holes_or_gaps": true|false, "single_feather": true|false, "fragment": true|false, "other_feather_inside": true|false, "other_material_inside": true|false, "model_score": <1-10: 10 = usable as is for measuring this feather, 1 = unusable>, "notes": "<at most 20 words: which check failed and where, or ok>"}

second_look._comment: When the first answer fails a check, ask again on the panel at `scale`; a check failed only once goes to review_uncertain instead of needs_review. Tested on the two 100-slide runs: the runs agree on the confirmed failures for 19 of 24 flagged feathers, against 8 of 24 with one look.

score._comment: judge_score = start minus each deduction for a failed check (side_cut per side marked cut; holes_or_gaps also when holes or a split mask are measured), at least min. For sorting and summaries only: needs_review, judge_segment_ok and the retry use the checks themselves. The model's own 1-10 answer is stored unused as judge_model_score. Measured holes (min_hole_frac and up) are recorded; they fail the holes check only from fail_hole_frac (2% of the feather): smaller ones are mostly natural vane splits.

repair._comment: Second sweep (src/feather_repair.py): a feather that failed a fixable check (outline cut, holes, material or glue inside, other feather inside) gets new masks (holes filled; SAM 3 interactive re-segmentation on the contrast-enhanced and the plain crop, box widened toward the cut sides), each checked again; one replaces the first mask only if it fails fewer checks and nothing new.

hidden._comment: Measured, not asked: a feather partly under the board, a card or another feather has ruler-straight stretches of outline (feather_judge.straight_outline, at `eps` px). Hidden when the runs crossing the feather (across_deg or more to its long axis) add up to across_frac of its length, or one run along it reaches along_frac (shorter runs along it are natural straight outer vanes and quill sides); 'most' when it is also smaller than most_max_rel_area of the slide's median feather. Deducts score.hidden_part / hidden_most and fails the check.

feather_judge._needs_support_comment: Model answers that only count as failures when a measurement backs them (feather_judge.demote_unsupported): holes_or_gaps (a measured hole of fail_hole_frac or a split mask), fragment (the clean-up marked the piece small or narrow). Otherwise listed in review_uncertain. From 50 hand verdicts: model-only holes flagged 4 good feathers and 0 bad.

regrow._comment: Measured outline cut on the left/right: SAM 3 re-segments each feather on a contrast-enhanced crop with its box widened by widen_frac on both sides; if the new mask grows by min_growth or more of the old one's area on a side (middle 15-75% of the length), that side is marked cut. Catches a pale vane on the white card that the first pass and the model miss.

inventory.prompt:
Reply with only the JSON object described at the end: no explanation, reasoning or text before or after it.

This is a scanned specimen slide with feathers. Every feather that the segmentation found is outlined in colour and labelled with a number in a white box; the numbers run 1, 2, 3 ... from left to right.

1. Count every feather on the slide, whole or partly hidden (under a card, board, tape or another feather). Count only feathers: not labels, text, tape, glue spots or shadows.
2. List every feather that has NO numbered outline. A feather counts as outlined if a numbered outline covers more than half of it. For each one, give the numbers of the outlined feathers directly to its left and right (null if there is none on that side) and its horizontal centre as a fraction of the image width (0 = left edge, 1 = right edge).

When you are unsure whether something is a separate feather or whether it is outlined, list it: a person checks every listed feather, while one you leave out is never looked at. If feathers overlap so much that you cannot tell how many there are, give your best count and say so in notes.

Answer with JSON only, no other text:
{"total_feathers": <integer>, "missed": [{"between": [<number or null>, <number or null>], "x_center": <0-1>, "partly_hidden": true|false}], "notes": "<at most 20 words>"}
Use "missed": [] when every feather is outlined.
